pages.text: These commands are mainly for server owners, test worlds, and development setups. Normal survival progression does not depend on them.$(br2)All commands begin with $(thing)/ramessescurse$(). Threat growth and selected testing controls are per-player.

pages.title: Guilt & Mercy
pages.text: $(li)/ramessescurse guilt set <player> <value>$(li)/ramessescurse guilt add <player> <value>$(li)/ramessescurse guilt remove <player> <value>$(li)/ramessescurse mercy set <player> <value>$(li)/ramessescurse mercy add <player> <value>$(li)/ramessescurse mercy remove <player> <value>$(br2)Useful for testing Curse V's maximum-Guilt punishment, Mercy progression, and stored death reversal.

pages.title: Threat Growth & Cooldown
pages.text: $(li)/ramessescurse dynasty_threat growth on [players]$(li)/ramessescurse dynasty_threat growth off [players]$(li)/ramessescurse cooling duat [player]$(li)/ramessescurse cooling edict [player]$(br2)Natural Dynasty Threat growth can be enabled or disabled per player. The growth switch only affects the daily increase; direct increases and dimension-change increases still work.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.text: If a curse does not progress as expected, verify three things:$(br)$(li)The Seal of Kadesh is equipped.$(li)The actual prerequisite is complete, such as suffering the maximum-Guilt punishment, defeating the specified boss or creature, or making the offering on the central End island.$(li)The client HUD and typewriter notice have synchronized.$(br2)Most apparent failures belong to one of these three cases.
